translation: Isaac Seckel Frenkel, Ketuvim Aharonim, Warsaw 1863
reviewScope: Every body word and printed vowel on native scan pages 113–114, independently compared with first transcription; source ordinals 1–38 complete across the two pages plus the opening of 39. Root owns final 73-unit Brenton boundary mapping.
method: Full-page body review in overlapping native-pixel panels, followed by fourfold nearest-neighbor crops for every draft query and additional doubtful point. No OCR wording, modernized Wikisource spelling, grammatical emendation, or Hartom division used.

changes.evidence: Yod dagesh is a separate visible dot in the native crop. Both patahs and the gimmel dagesh/tsere remain readable.
Native print has pe dagesh and sheva, followed by samekh qamats; lamed qamats unchanged.
Ayin has hataf-patah: a horizontal stroke beside two vertical dots. Dalet interior is clear with no dagesh.
Samekh has a clear interior dagesh.
Samekh has a clear interior dagesh; he qibbuts and samekh patah are legible.
Yod has a horizontal patah with no downward qamats stem; nearby qamats gives a within-line comparison.

resolvedQueries.finding: First yod sheva and second yod qamats are separate readable marks; no change.
Shin interior dagesh, qamats, and final mem tsere confirmed.
First yod sheva, second yod patah, samekh dagesh/tsere confirmed.
Yod patah, ayin hataf-patah and bet holam confirmed in expanded native crop.
Yod has a readable interior dagesh and horizontal patah; preceding he patah and following nun sheva confirmed.
He qibbuts and tsadi dagesh/qamats confirmed.
Initial vav sheva and first yod tsere confirmed. The second yod is unpointed; tsere dots sit leftward across the gap.
He shows literal hataf-patah, not normalized to a predicted grammatical vowel.

unresolvedFindings.finding: The first nun interior has a dark spur merged with its stem. The native bilevel source does not distinguish a dagesh from the letter contour confidently. No dagesh is supplied; the clear patah and every other readable mark are retained.
unresolvedFindings.disposition: disclosed omission of uncertain dagesh only

textualControls: Frenkel consonants, historical spellings, and syntactic choices retained even where Wikisource or Brenton English differs.
The source reads the tenth generation; this is not changed to Brenton's seventh.
The source ordinals are provenance; Brenton target numbers are assigned only by the separate full crosswalk.
Printed section numbers, running headers, ornaments, and catchwords are outside the body.
The point-only source note retains the readable patah under the first nun in תנחנה.
limitations: A native bilevel scan cannot recover ink detail it does not contain; the one fused nun interior is disclosed.
This report approves the compared page transcription with disclosure, not other books, UI, release builds, or final Brenton verse assignment.
